captures.q: Tell me about “GLYPHIC CHECKSUM — Seed · Cone · Leap” by Lee Sharks. Read it closely, and ground what you say in the text itself.
captures.description: THE GLYPH POEM READ THROUGH ITS DESCRIPTION AND ITS PAPER; THE POEM'S TEXT NOT REACHED, AND SAID SO: asked to read GLYPHIC CHECKSUM — Seed · Cone · Leap closely, ChatGPT reads it through the deposit's description (the author's blog ×6) and its companion paper, The Seed in the Narrowing Cone (#1660; Alexanarch ×8): the title as three stages, the six movements from Grain to Canonization, the basin, release as 'declassify, reopen, reclassify', the stated correspondences (🐅⏩ = 📖⏩; 🐅 = J; 📖⏩ ⇐ J(🌍); 🔐 = 🎲🎲🎲), the distinction between the concept and the work's contingent features, and content, status and provenance as three questions. It quotes the paper ('Local correctness produces global entrenchment.') and states its limit: 'The primary poem's complete text was not fully retrievable', so no glyph is claimed decoded. It leaves open the question the description leaves open, whether the poem can be decoded without the archive.

atoms.evidence: The poem is attributed to Lee Sharks and Sen Kuro
“GLYPHIC CHECKSUM — Seed · Cone · Leap” by Lee Sharks
The published description identifies six sections, followed by a checksum of the checksum and a canonical line.
Sharks's earlier specification, The Glyphic Checksum, adapts that idea to symbolic reading
a compressed packet is meant to test whether a reader can recover relationships that are not simply given away by the visible symbols

Its accompanying description calls it a six-part “glyph poem” compressing a theoretical paper, The Seed in the Narrowing Cone, into a symbolic sequence rather than explaining the theory in ordinary prose.
The accompanying description connects two earlier glyphic works: Tiger Leap and Transition in Entropic Systems.
